snapshot.what_it_does: Bajaj Finance Limited (BFL) is a listed Indian financial services company whose annual report is for FY2026 (year ended 31 March 2026). The provided pages are the AGM notice and related shareholder communications; they indicate the company is a lender that borrows from banks, financial institutions and via debentures/bonds/commercial papers and fixed/corporate deposits, and that Bajaj Housing Finance Limited is its subsidiary.

segments.name: Business segments
segments.note: The provided pages do not describe any operating or reportable segments.

snapshot.geographies: India (registered and corporate offices in Pune, Maharashtra; listed on BSE and NSE). No other geographies are stated.
key_facts: Recommended dividend of ₹6 per equity share of face value ₹1 for FY2026, including a special payout of ₹0.60 per share from an exceptional gain on sale of shares of subsidiary Bajaj Housing Finance Limited (p11)
Borrowing powers proposed to be increased to ₹550,000 crore (p3)
Charge/security creation on assets proposed up to ₹550,000 crore (p4)
Material related party transactions with Bajaj Housing Finance Limited approved up to ₹18,152 crore for the RPT period (p3)

39th AGM to be held on 30 July 2026 via VC/OAVM; Rajiv Bajaj to retire and not seek re-appointment; Pramit Jhaveri proposed for re-appointment as Independent Director for a second five-year term from 1 August 2026 (p2-3)

promised_vs_delivered.verdict: Credibility looks strong so far: H1 FY27 actuals met or beat guidance on credit cost, ROA/ROE, AUM and customer adds, with AUM and customer guidance raised. The one clear miss is MSME, still at +3% in Q2 FY27 versus a promised return to double-digit growth; most full-year FY27 targets are not yet reported.

bull.point: Profit momentum is strong: Q2 FY27 PAT ₹6,266 cr, +28.5% YoY after Q1 +27.4%; FY26 Q4 was +22.0%.
Execution credibility high: H1 FY27 credit cost 1.54-1.56%, ROA 4.6-4.7%, ROE 20.4-20.6% met/beat FY27 guidance ranges.
Growth raised: Q2 FY27 AUM +26.5% to ₹5,84,624 cr; FY27 AUM guidance lifted to 26-27%, customer target to 18-20 mn.

bear.point: MSME is the clear miss: promised double-digit growth by Q2-Q3 FY27, but Q2 FY27 grew only +3% after Q4 FY26 +6%.
Earnings are not linear: Q3 FY26 PAT fell 6.3% YoY to ₹3,978 cr, showing downside despite the FY27 rebound.
Balance-sheet reliance is heavy: borrowing/security powers proposed to ₹550,000 cr, plus Bajaj Housing Finance RPTs approved up to ₹18,152 cr.

watch: MSME growth: whether it moves from +3% in Q2 FY27 back to the promised double-digit trajectory.
Full-year FY27 delivery versus credit cost 145-160 bps, ROA 4.4-4.6%, ROE 19-20%, and raised AUM/customer guidance.
Gold loan scale-up toward ~5% of AUM and ₹29,000-31,000 cr, plus evidence of 25-40 bps opex-to-NTI improvement.
